title: JSON parse/stringify and data limitations
learningObjectives: Explain json parse/stringify and data limitations and read or transform JavaScript data safely.

understand.concept: JSON is a text data format with objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, and null. JSON.stringify converts supported JavaScript values to JSON text; JSON.parse converts valid JSON text into JavaScript values. JSON does not preserve functions, undefined object properties, symbols, or object identity, and it cannot represent circular references.
understand.whyItMatters: JSON is common for APIs and stored data. Validate parsed data against an expected schema before trusting it, and handle parsing errors. Serialization is not a secure cloning or validation boundary.
understand.analogy: JSON is a portable written form of data; parsing reads it into values, while stringifying writes values into the format.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript references, serialization, and DOM APIs have precise behaviour defined by the language and web platform.

explain.narrative: The object becomes JSON text and is parsed back into a new object with the same supported data values.

examples.explanation: The object becomes JSON text and is parsed back into a new object with the same supported data values.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console or page displays the selected, transformed, or serialized data.

practise.guidedTask: Serialize an object, parse it back, and test what happens to undefined and a function property. Catch invalid JSON errors.
practise.independentTask: Build a small data-processing or DOM-selection example. Include missing-data handling and explain any shallow-copy or serialization limits.
hints: Check optional properties before accessing them.
Remember shallow copies share nested references.
Handle JSON parsing errors and validate data shape.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>JSON parse/stringify and data limitations</title></head><body>
<script>const lesson={id:'H1',title:'HTML basics',complete:true};const text=JSON.stringify(lesson);const parsed=JSON.parse(text);console.log(text,parsed.title);</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which method converts valid JSON text into a JavaScript value?
questions.explanation: JSON.parse() parses JSON text into a JavaScript value.

questions.prompt: What is a safe approach when working with nested or external data?
options: Check structure and handle missing or invalid values
Use JSON parsing as schema validation
questions.answer: Check structure and handle missing or invalid values
questions.explanation: External data must be checked for expected shape and valid values.
